security_audit.summary: All static alerts were adjudicated as false positives because they occur in Markdown documentation, placeholders, official Telegram links, or example code. No evidence of prompt injection, malicious command execution, credential exfiltration, or hidden binary content was found in the cited files.

remediation.issue: The examples mention tokens, .env files, and API hashes as part of normal Telegram setup.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note near each setup example that real secrets must stay out of source control and public prompts.

remediation.issue: Some Mini App examples print user, location, or token-like values for demonstration.
remediation.suggestion: Use redacted sample output and state that production apps should avoid logging personal or sensitive data.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences and placeholder URLs trigger automated marketplace scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples fenced, label placeholders clearly, and document that examples are not executed by the skill.

content.user_title: Build Telegram Bots and Mini Apps
content.value_statement: Telegram projects require many APIs and platform rules. This skill gives focused guidance for bots, Mini Apps, webhooks, payments, and client libraries.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bot API setup, token use, polling, and webhook flows.
Shows inline keyboards, reply keyboards, command menus, and callback handling.
Covers Mini Apps initialization, UI controls, storage APIs, and initData validation.
Summarizes TDLib, MTProto client options, and official Telegram resources.
Provides message formatting guidance for aligned Telegram tables and data views.
limitations: It does not create live bot tokens or register Telegram apps.
Examples are templates and still need production review.
It does not deploy infrastructure or validate a live webhook endpoint.
It does not replace the official Telegram documentation for API changes.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Telegram bot
use_cases.description: Plan a simple bot that replies to messages, handles commands, and uses safe token storage.

use_cases.title: Design a Mini App workflow
use_cases.description: Map a Telegram Mini App flow with native buttons, storage choices, payments, and initData validation.

use_cases.title: Format bot data messages
use_cases.description: Create readable Telegram message layouts for rankings, tables, balances, and status reports.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to outline a simple Telegram bot that replies to text messages. Include setup steps and security notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add interactive buttons
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to design inline buttons, reply keyboards, and command menus for my bot. Explain when each option fits best.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Mini App flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to plan a Telegram Mini App with native UI controls, storage, payment entry points, and server-side initData validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to review my Telegram bot deployment plan. Cover webhooks, token handling, admin checks, rate limits, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: I need a bot menu for settings, reports, and support.
output: Recommended pattern: use inline buttons for contextual actions.
Use a reply keyboard for frequent shortcuts that should stay visible.
Use the command menu for global actions such as help and settings.

output_examples.input: I want to launch a Mini App from my bot.
output: Start with a secure HTTPS URL and register the entry point in Telegram.
Validate initData on the server before trusting user identity or payments.
Keep sensitive secrets on the server, not in the Mini App client.

output_examples.input: My bot should send a readable leaderboard.
output_examples.output: The skill can recommend fixed-width formatting, aligned columns, short number labels, and mobile-friendly message sections.

best_practices: Store real bot tokens in environment variables and keep them out of source control.
Validate Telegram Mini App initData on the server before processing user actions.
Use webhooks with HTTPS for production bots and add timeout handling for API calls.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real bot tokens, API hashes, or payment secrets in examples or source files.
Do not trust initDataUnsafe or client-supplied user data without server-side checks.
Do not expose admin actions without explicit user ID or role validation.

faq.question: Does this skill run a Telegram bot for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You still run, deploy, and secure the bot yourself.

faq.question: Can it help with Telegram Mini Apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers initialization, UI controls, storage, payments, launch options, and initData validation.

faq.question: Does it include MTProto guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It summarizes TDLib and MTProto client development options and links to official resources.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it provide production security advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes token handling, webhook requirements, initData validation, and admin permission checks.

faq.question: Are the examples complete production applications?
faq.answer: No. They are implementation templates that need testing, monitoring, and project-specific hardening.
